title and abstract.summary: This study quantified body size variation in the species Halictus ligatus across three different urban cities to compare the variation between bees residing in these distinct environments. This study measured the body size variation (head width and intertegular distance) in female Halictus ligatus across three different Midwestern United States cities and assessed the relationship between this body size and temperature.

introduction.summary: This study quantified and compared body size variation in the facultatively eusocial sweat bee species, Halictus ligatus, across three distinct Midwestern cities to determine if body size variation patterns were conserved or diverged among these urban landscapes. This study measured the body size variation in the sweat bee Halictus ligatus across populations sampled from three different cities in the Midwestern United States (Chicago, Detroit, and Saint Louis), and investigated how climate factors might influence this variation. methods.summary: The study measured the head width and intertegular distance of 240 Hylaeus ligatus females collected from community gardens in three Midwestern US cities. The study measured the head width and intertegular distance of female Hylaeus ligatus to assess their relationship with overall body size and to compare these measurements across three different urban populations.

results.summary: This study measured the body size variation of female Halictus ligatus collected across three Midwestern cities (Chicago, Detroit, and Saint Louis) between May and October of 2016. The study measured the variation in head width of Hylaeus ligatus bees across three different surveyed cities (Chicago, Detroit, and Saint Louis) and across different seasons. This study measured the variation in body size of female Halictus ligatus sweat bees across different months and cities.

discussion.summary: This study measured the body size variation in the social sweat bee, Halictus ligatus, across three geographically separated urban cities: Chicago, Detroit, and Saint Louis. This study measured the body size variation of Halictus ligatus bees across three distinct urban systems to assess the role of seasonality and temperature on this variation. The study measured the body size variation of Hylaeus ligatus bees residing in natural areas and in cities with known elevated $ ext{CO}_2$ levels, and analyzed the pollen nutrient content from plants in urban spaces.
